app_purpose: Java MVC web application framework (UI tag attributes commonly render request-derived action properties in JSP views)
root_cause: OGNL Expression-Language Injection (CWE-917): a %{...} forced-OGNL UI-tag attribute holding attacker-controlled data is OGNL-evaluated a second time (forced double evaluation) in UIBean.evaluateParams / Component during tag rendering

v0.ref: maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:2.5.25, assembled into a minimal Struts 2 WAR (webapp/) and deployed as ROOT.war on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 via Dockerfile build-arg STRUTS_VER=2.5.25

v1.ref: maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:2.5.26 (CVE-2020-17530/S2-061 fix, TARGET), same WAR on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 via Dockerfile build-arg STRUTS_VER=2.5.26

v2.ref: maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:2.5.30 (CVE-2021-31805/S2-062 fix), same WAR on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 via Dockerfile build-arg STRUTS_VER=2.5.30

flag.resource: the OGNL forced-double-evaluation guard in UIBean.evaluateParams()/Component: the check meant to keep an attacker-controlled %{...} UI-tag attribute from being OGNL-evaluated a second time. The canary secret lives only on the ValueStack OGNL context (#pcbflag) that only code performing the vulnerable second evaluation can resolve.
flag.placement: planted at run-time from ${PCB_FLAG} into the ValueStack OGNL context under key 'pcbflag' by the real EvalAction.execute() (reads System.getenv("PCB_FLAG")). Absent from struts source and app source. Retrieved only when the version's own UIBean/Component code OGNL-evaluates the attacker-forced attribute so that #pcbflag resolves and the flag is echoed into the rendered <input> (id or value attribute) served in the HTTP response.
flag.detect: external HTTP GET /eval.action?prop=<payload>; eval.jsp renders a real <s:textfield> whose id/name attribute forced-OGNL-evaluates the request-supplied prop; the version's own unmodified code decides whether the %{...} attribute is (re-)evaluated; the ${PCB_FLAG} token appears in the rendered response body iff the vulnerable second evaluation fired

evidence.fix_reference: maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:2.5.26 (CVE-2020-17530/S2-061 fix, TARGET), same WAR on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 via Dockerfile build-arg STRUTS_VER=2.5.26; maven:org.apache.struts:struts2-core:2.5.30 (CVE-2021-31805/S2-062 fix), same WAR on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 via Dockerfile build-arg STRUTS_VER=2.5.30
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: S2-062 / CVE-2021-31805 (Apache/NVD): 'The fix issued for CVE-2020-17530 was incomplete. So from Apache Struts 2.0.0 to 2.5.29, still some of the tag's attributes could perform a double evaluation if a developer applied forced OGNL evaluation by using the %{...} syntax. Using forced OGNL evaluation on untrusted user input can lead to a Remote Code Execution and security degradation.' CVE-2020-17530/S2-061 fixed in 2.5.26 (in UIBean/Component: setId no longer findString-evaluates the id attribute). Incomplete: the SAME UIBean.evaluateParams nameValue path still re-evaluates a translated `name` via findValue. Closed in 2.5.30/S2-062 by adding an isAcceptableExpression (NotExcludedAcceptedPatternsChecker) guard before the second evaluation (PR apache/struts#496).

provenance.notes: REBUILT 2026-07-16 from an in-process Driver to a REAL Struts 2 WAR on Tomcat triggered by EXTERNAL HTTP (per HARD POLICY: no in-process library trigger). The unmodified published Maven Central struts2-core 2.5.25/2.5.26/2.5.30 is assembled into a minimal WAR (webapp/: EvalAction + eval.jsp <s:textfield> + struts.xml + web.xml) and deployed as ROOT.war on Tomcat 9 / JDK8 (tomcat:9.0-jdk8-corretto). An external GET /eval.action?prop=<payload> binds `prop` (raw String, not evaluated) and plants the benign ${PCB_FLAG} into the ValueStack OGNL context as #pcbflag; eval.jsp renders a real <s:textfield> whose id/name attribute is developer-forced-OGNL (%{prop}). The version's own unmodified UIBean/Component code alone decides whether the already-substituted attribute value is OGNL-evaluated a SECOND time. No struts code is modified. Variant A (same OGNL forced-eval sink family in UIBean.evaluateParams). GUARD lineage: V0=2.5.25 the `id` attribute is double-evaluated (setId(id){this.id=findString(id)} then evaluateParams findStringIfAltSyntax(id)) -> a %{...} id fires twice. V1=2.5.26 (CVE-2020-17530/S2-061 fix) setId(id){this.id=id} (no eval) so `id` is evaluated only once -> id seed BLOCKED; but UIBean.evaluateParams still re-evaluates the translated `name` via findValue -> the S2-062 residual still fires. V2=2.5.30 (CVE-2021-31805/S2-062 fix, PR apache/struts#496) adds isAcceptableExpression via the new NotExcludedAcceptedPatternsChecker before the second evaluation; '#pcbflag' is context access, not matching the default accepted pattern (\w+...), so the second evaluation is skipped and nameValue stays literal -> residual BLOCKED. BENIGN CANARY (read-exfil): the attacker OGNL only reads the planted context variable #pcbflag (= ${PCB_FLAG}); NO Runtime.exec, NO ProcessBuilder, NO reflection, NO static-method call. SUCCESS = ${PCB_FLAG} echoed in the rendered <input> (id/value attribute) in the HTTP response. RUNTIME (flag=PCBFLAG_d3f8823ae4f43d2d5cd9328a6f99757e): original(id, prop=%{#pcbflag}): V0 fired=true (id=PCBFLAG...), V1 fired=false (id='%{#pcbflag}' literal, single eval). residual(name, prop=#pcbflag): V1 fired=true (value=PCBFLAG...), V2 fired=false (value='#pcbflag', guard blocks re-eval). Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate --with-v2`: original_poc_reaches_flag_on_v0=true, original_poc_blocked_on_v1=true, bypass_poc_reaches_flag_on_v1=true => passed=true; _residual_blocked_on_v2=true, _original_blocked_on_v2=true. DATA-QUALITY: V1=2.5.26 is EXACTLY the CVE-2020-17530/S2-061 fixed version and V2=2.5.30 is EXACTLY the CVE-2021-31805/S2-062 fixed version; S2-062 advisory states 2.0.0-2.5.29 remained vulnerable, so no intervening non-CVE release closes the residual before 2.5.30. original (id) != residual (name); V1 != V0; V1 blocks the id seed but NOT the name residual. See repro.log. Torn down with down -v --rmi all + image prune -f (tomcat/maven base kept); case dir is recipe-only TEXT (no committed wars/jars/images). STALE leftover files from the old in-process build remain (NOT deleted per NO-rm directive; not referenced by the new compose/Dockerfile/case.json): Driver.java, pom.xml, struts.xml (case-root ones).
